content:
Searching for a JEE Maths DPP PDF that covers the whole syllabus in one file? Most free sheets online hand you 20 random questions and no solutions. So our 30 Practice Papers PDF fixes that gap. It packs 900 solved questions. All 30 chapters sit inside. Grab the free 20-question mock below first. Then download the full set.

What a good JEE Maths DPP PDF holds

  • One paper per chapter, so no topic slips through the cracks.
  • A worked solution for every question, not just an answer key.
  • A difficulty ramp from JEE Main warm-ups to Advanced posers.
  • A clean printable layout you can solve away from a screen.
  • A fixed question count per paper for honest timed practice.

Why chapter-wise DPPs beat random sets

Random question dumps feel productive. But they hide your weak chapters. A chapter-wise paper forces one topic at a time. So you find the exact unit that leaks marks. Then you fix it fast. Random practice never gives you that clean signal. A focused paper does.

How to use the 30 papers

Solve one paper in a single timed sitting. Mark every question you miss. Then read its solution and note the reason. Redo the missed ones two days later. Also keep a short error log as you go. That loop turns a flat PDF into real marks.

questions.q: Consider the set A = {x : x is a rational number and x² = 2}. Set A is a:
questions.explanation: x² = 2 gives x = ±√2, both irrational. No rational number qualifies, so A is empty.

questions.q: Two finite sets have m and n elements. The number of subsets of the first is 56 more than the second. Then m and n are:
questions.explanation: Subsets satisfy 2^m - 2^n = 56 = 2³(2³ - 1). Matching the factors gives n = 3 and m = 6.

questions.q: The quadratic equation f(x) = x² - 6x + 8 has both roots in the interval:
questions.explanation: Factor x² - 6x + 8 = (x - 2)(x - 4). The roots 2 and 4 both lie inside (0, 4).

questions.q: If x² + bx + c = 0 has rational roots and b, c are integers, then which must be true?
options: b and c are both even.
questions.explanation: With integer b and c, the roots are rational only when the discriminant b² - 4c is a perfect square.

questions.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word 'EQUATION' be arranged so that all the vowels stay together?
questions.explanation: Tie the 5 vowels as one block: 4! ways for the units and 5! inside. So 24 × 120 = 2880.

questions.q: There are 10 lamps in a hall, each switched on independently. The number of ways to illuminate the hall is:
questions.explanation: Each lamp is on or off, giving 2^10 states. Remove the all-off case: 1024 - 1 = 1023.

questions.q: The value of 2C2 + 3C2 + 4C2 + 5C2 is equal to:
questions.explanation: By the hockey-stick identity, 2C2 + 3C2 + 4C2 + 5C2 = 6C3.

questions.q: The constant term in the expansion of (1 + x)ⁿ (1 + 1/x)ⁿ is:
questions.explanation: (1 + x)ⁿ (1 + 1/x)ⁿ = (1 + x)²ⁿ / xⁿ. The constant term is the coefficient of xⁿ, which is 2nCn.

questions.q: Which row operation preserves the determinant of a matrix?
options: Multiplying a row by a scalar
Adding a multiple of one row to another
questions.explanation: Adding a multiple of one row to another leaves the determinant unchanged. Swapping flips its sign and scaling multiplies it.

questions.q: If A is an invertible matrix of order 2, then det(A⁻¹) equals:
questions.explanation: Since A·A⁻¹ = I, we get |A||A⁻¹| = 1. So det(A⁻¹) = 1/det(A).

questions.q: A chord of a circle of radius 7 lies at distance 5 from the centre. Its length is:
questions.explanation: Half-chord = √(49 - 25) = √24. So the full chord is 2√24.

questions.q: The tangents to x² + y² = 25 that are parallel to the line 3x - 4y = 0 are:
questions.explanation: A tangent sits at distance 5 from the centre. Parallel to 3x - 4y = 0, this gives 3x - 4y = ±25.

questions.q: Evaluate lim(x→0) (1 - cos x) / x².
questions.explanation: Write 1 - cos x = 2 sin²(x/2). The limit reduces to 2 × (1/4) = 1/2.

questions.q: Evaluate lim(x→∞) (3x² + 5x - 1) / (2x² - 3).
questions.explanation: Top and bottom share the same degree, so the limit is the ratio of leading coefficients, 3/2.

questions.q: The value of ∫ from 0 to 1 of 1/(1 + x²) dx is:
questions.explanation: The antiderivative is arctan x. From 0 to 1 it gives arctan 1 = π/4.

questions.q: Using properties of definite integrals, ∫ from 0 to π/2 of sin x/(sin x + cos x) dx equals:
questions.explanation: Apply the a-minus-x property and add the two forms. Then 2I = π/2, so I = π/4.

questions.q: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 100. The probability that it is divisible by 3 or 5 is:
questions.explanation: Multiples of 3 are 33, of 5 are 20, of 15 are 6. So 33 + 20 - 6 = 47, giving 47/100.

questions.q: Three coins are tossed. The probability of all heads given that at least two heads appeared is:
questions.explanation: At least two heads has 4 outcomes, and all heads is 1 of them. So the probability is 1/4.

questions.q: If |a + b| = |a - b| for two non-zero vectors a and b, then they are:
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides cancels the magnitudes and leaves 4 a·b = 0. So a and b are perpendicular.
